commits.pr_title: fix(browser): check mock path boundaries (fix #11361)
commits.pr_body:
### Description

With the root at `packages/app`, `resolveMockPath()` turns `/@fs/.../packages/app-utils/src/value.ts` into `-utils/src/value.ts`, and the Playwright provider never intercepts the request.

It now checks `withTrailingSlash(root)` like `node/resolver.ts` does. `slice()` still uses the root length. A root of `/` behaves as before.

Resolves #11361

I added a `project1-utils` directory next to `project1` in the `mocking-out-of-root` fixture. Without the fix, the import gets `"project1-utils"` instead of the mock.

I used Claude Code to find the cause and write the patch. I reviewed the change myself.

commits.message:
fix: isolate `result.status` between `repeats` runs (#11218)

Co-authored-by: Hiroshi Ogawa <4232207+hi-ogawa@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Codex (GPT-6) <noreply@openai.com>
commits.author: hi-ogawa
commits.pr_title: fix: isolate `result.status` between `repeats` runs
commits.pr_body:
### Description

While looking into `test.fails + retry` oddity https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/11068, found something unusual with `repeats` too. 

The repeats loop currently reuses `result.state` between iterations. For example, this causes a successful repeat after a failure to trigger `onTestFailed`. For another example with `retry` enabled, a later successful repeat can erase failures from earlier repeats and report the test as passed.

This PR resets the result for each repeat and collects failed repeat errors separately, so each repeat is evaluated independently and any failed repeat keeps the overall test failed.

commits.message: fix(vitest): remove root temp dir on close (#11248)
commits.author: abhinav-phi
commits.pr_title: fix(vitest): remove root temp dir on close
commits.pr_body:
### Description

A fully green run leaks the root `Vitest._tmpDir` under `os.tmpdir()`. The core workspace project shares the root fetcher (`TestProject._createBasicProject` assigns `vitest._fetcher`), so the per-run tmp module copies land in the root temp directory, but only the per-project `TestProject.tmpDir` is removed by `TestProject.close()`. `Vitest.close()` removes nothing.

This mirrors the per-project pattern: `Vitest.close()` now removes the root temp directory after the projects and the pool are down (`_clearTmpDir()`, guarded against a missing path and repeated `close()`). Since `_setRootConfig()` re-creates the fetcher, a restart after a closed run allocates a fresh directory instead of pointing at a deleted path.

Regression test (`test/node-runner/test/root-tmpdir.test.js`): runs a tiny fixture with the forks pool while `os.tmpdir()` is redirected into a private sandbox, and asserts the sandbox is empty again after `close()`. It fails on current `main` (the leaked nanoid directory is listed) and passes with this change.

Fixes #11224 — intent noted in https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/11224#issuecomment-5642417138

Opened by @abhinav-phi; implementation was assisted by an AI coding agent (ZCode), per the disclosure in CONTRIBUTING.md.

### Note on the `Test: unit, node-24, windows-latest` check

This leg can fail on the `test/ui` `suite report navigation` flake (coordinate-based explorer-row clicks racing the virtual scroller) — the same failure appears on `main` and unrelated PRs, and the fix is in #11236. It is unrelated to this change; once #11236 merges, this PR's checks pick the fix up through the merge ref.

commits.message: fix(cache): revalidate imports of cached modules (#11381)
commits.author: sheremet-va
commits.pr_title: fix(cache): revalidate imports of cached modules
commits.pr_body:
A cached transform imports the urls that Vite resolved when the module was transformed. The cache now checks that every import still resolves to the same module before serving the entry, and re-transforms the module otherwise, for example after a dependency was renamed on a branch switch.

Cached importers also register their out-of-root imports as safe to load, as import analysis does, so a client environment (jsdom, happy-dom) can load a changed dependency outside `server.fs.allow`.

No noticeable performance or memory regression: measured with vitest-dev/benchmarks (node-library, barrel-hell, enterprise-monolith, react-spa) and interleaved A/B runs of the warm cache cells. Wall time and peak RSS are within noise; the cache on disk grows by about 1%.

Fixes #11246
closes https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11254 (supersedes)

commits.message: fix(pool): preserve unique pool ids when `groupOrder` is set (#11392)
commits.author: mtorp
commits.pr_title: fix(pool): preserve unique pool ids when `groupOrder` is set
commits.pr_body:
### Description

> Written with Claude Code (an AI agent) on behalf of @mtorp, who has reviewed it.

`setMaxWorkers()` replaces `workerIds` when the next `sequence.groupOrder` group starts. The last task of the previous group frees its id after that, so the free lands in the new map and marks an id as free while it is still in use. The next file then runs with the same `VITEST_POOL_ID`. This change frees each id into the map it was taken from.

Resolves #11391

fix(vm): do not optimize deps from index.html (fix #11329) (#11360)

Co-authored-by: Hiroshi Ogawa <4232207+hi-ogawa@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: ezefernandezyf
commits.pr_title: fix(vm): do not optimize deps from index.html (fix #11329)
commits.pr_body:
### Description

- closes #11329

_description by @hi-ogawa_

Since Vitest switched from vite-node to module runner https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/8208, the vm runner is using custom `__vitest_vm__` environment with `client` consumer, but it was missing optimize dep config patching, which disabled dependency auto discovery of client environment. This PR lifts up that logic, so it also applies to `__vitest_vm__` environment. 

---

_original description_

With `pool: 'vmThreads'` or `'vmForks'`, Vite's dependency optimizer runs over the project's `index.html` import graph. If a dependency reached from `index.html` cannot be bundled, the run ends with an unhandled rejection and exit code 1, even when every test passes and no test imports that dependency. The same project with `pool: 'threads'` exits 0.

I reproduced it with a fixture of my own (a project `index.html` that reaches a dependency the bundler cannot parse, plus one unrelated passing test):

| variant | exit |
| --- | --- |
| `vmThreads`, `vmForks` | 1 |
| `threads`, `forks` | 0 |
| `vmThreads`, `index.html` removed | 0 |
| `vmThreads` + `environments.__vitest_vm__.optimizeDeps.noDiscovery` | 0 |

### Root cause

The `configEnvironment` handler in `packages/vitest/src/node/plugins/runnerTransform.ts` returns early for `__vitest_vm__` before applying `resolveOptimizerConfig`, so the environment keeps Vite's client default and discovers dependencies from every `index.html`.

That early return reads as being about externalization (`resolve.external` / `noExternal`), which the vm environment does not use because it loads modules with the native import mechanism. It also covers `optimizeDeps` though, which is a separate concern. `__vitest_vm__` is the only environment in that skip list with `consumer: 'client'`; `__vitest__` has no consumer, so Vite treats it as a server and never reads `index.html`.

As far as I can tell this arrived with #9508.

fix(expect): pass current equality testers to `expect.extend` asymmetric matchers (#11401)

Co-authored-by: Hiroshi Ogawa <4232207+hi-ogawa@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: hi-ogawa
commits.pr_title: fix(expect): pass current equality testers to `expect.extend` asymmetric matchers
commits.pr_body:
- follow-up to https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/6825
- related to https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/11296

#6825 forwarded the outer matcher's equality testers to built-in asymmetric matchers, but not to ones created via `expect.extend` (e.g. `expect.toBeOneOf`). This PR forwards them there too.

```ts
class Stock { constructor(public type: string) {} }

// already fails since #6825
expect([new Set()]).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining([new Set(['x'])]))
expect([new Stock('x')]).toStrictEqual(expect.arrayContaining([{ type: 'x' }]))

// passes before this PR, fails after
expect(new Set()).toEqual(expect.toBeOneOf([new Set(['x'])]))
expect(new Stock('x')).toStrictEqual(expect.toBeOneOf([{ type: 'x' }]))
```

Non-asymmetric `expect(new Set()).toBeOneOf([new Set(['x'])])` still passes (i.e. broken), but that's left for #11296.

fix(vm): don't reuse scripts across vite environments (#11395)

Signed-off-by: Martin Oehlert <453360+MO2k4@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Martin Oehlert <453360+MO2k4@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: MO2k4
commits.pr_title: fix(vm): don't reuse scripts across vite environments
commits.pr_body:
### Description

Written by an AI agent (Claude) on behalf of @MO2k4, who has reviewed it.

The vm pools cache compiled scripts of inlined modules per worker (#10744), keyed only by module id. A worker can run both `jsdom` files (`client` environment) and `node` files (`ssr` environment), which transform the same id differently: for example, optimized deps resolve to `deps/` in one and `deps_ssr/` in the other. The second environment then evaluates the first one's code. This shows up as `vi.mock` not being applied and as duplicate module instances (`instanceof` failing), and it depends on the order files land on workers.

The cache now also stores the code and reuses a script only when the code matches, the same way `CodeCache` already works for externalized modules.

Bisected on a real suite: `de63174f5` is clean and `d8b040c63` (#10744) fails. With this change, that suite is green in 3 of 3 runs, compared with 13–31 failures per run on 5.0.2.

Resolves #11289
